resources.string: Open a protected Debian VM inside Android’s Terminal app.
Ready. The launcher is available for 30 minutes while idle.
Unavailable. Check root permission and that the stock Terminal is installed. Root must support su -M.
Disabled. No VM will be launched.
Not connected. Enable this module in Vector, select Terminal as its only scope, and reopen this app.
Terminal is not in the Vector scope.
Scope configured. Open Terminal to load the module.
Module loaded in Terminal. Successful Linux startup is shown in its console.
Connect Terminal to the protected VM
Changes apply when Terminal is reopened. Turning this off restores its original behavior, which may not support this device.
Close all guest sessions and stop the VM. Save your work first. The private Linux disk is retained.
Stopped. Prepare the launcher before opening Terminal again.
Could not confirm shutdown. Check root permission.
The stock Terminal is missing or disabled.

RAM, CPUs, lifetime and keep-alive are configurable; storage only grows through a verified copy. Stock networking uses a proxy and explicit UDP/ping. The custom kernel also supports optional guest TUN for ordinary TCP/UDP/DNS. Direct USB, GPU Vulkan and hardware video remain unavailable.

Android’s kernel, boot partitions and SELinux stay unchanged; no Android reboot. Choose stock Microdroid or a verified guest image in private app storage. Root and Gunyah are required. This route has no pvmfw verified boot or equivalent AVF guarantee.

1. Use the buttons above to enable Terminal and open its Linux installer.
2. In Vector, enable this module for Terminal only.
3. Allow root here, then open Terminal.
First startup creates a private Linux disk. For a software desktop, run plb-install-gui in Terminal, then use its display button.
Terminal and its installer are enabled.
Could not enable Terminal. Check root permission and whether this OS includes the stock Terminal.
This OS or Terminal version is untested. The bridge is disabled for compatibility.

Network egress uses the selected Android app UID and its INTERNET permission, VPN and power policy. Terminal is the default; the experimental profile can explicitly choose Bridge for its fullscreen GUI. Background/Doze restrictions can block either app. No host routes, DNS, firewall or power restrictions are changed.

Run plb-install-gpu inside Linux, then save graphics settings here and recreate only the VM. Android restart is unnecessary. virgl (Adreno) in plb-gpu-info indicates host GPU OpenGL. Weston composition and direct Android GPU viewing have separate switches. Capture and copying still use CPU. Zero-copy and GPU Vulkan are not supported.

ping -c 4 1.1.1.1 sends real IPv4 echo requests without raw sockets. plb-udp-forward 5353 1.1.1.1 53 forwards guest localhost:5353 to the specified UDP destination until interrupted. Configure your tool to use that local port. This is explicit forwarding, not transparent networking. Host-local, link-local and multicast destinations are blocked.

Resolution, frame-rate cap and Linux graphics apply at the next VM start. Reopen the viewer to change display transport. First run plb-install-gpu inside Linux. Saved Bridge settings override guest mode commands at VM startup. The fps selection is an upper limit; actual speed depends on the display, VM and application.
This closes all Linux sessions. Save your Linux work first. Android will not restart.
Bridge has no saved GPU override; the existing settings inside Linux are preserved.
Could not apply settings. Check root permission and enable the Bridge.
Saved Bridge settings are loaded. Running VM state may differ until recreated.
Saved. Linux graphics apply at the next VM start; reopen the display for the display option.
Applied. The VM was recreated and Terminal reopened.
Saved the display option. Close and reopen the display to apply; no VM restart needed.

Linux root and sudo apply inside the VM. Android files are not shared. The GPU decoder is unprivileged, but the host VMM currently runs as root without its normal process sandbox. This is not a fully hardened environment for untrusted code; host/hypervisor/GPU bugs may affect Android.
Keep the VM after closing all views
Boot actual systemd for service management

Applied at the next VM start. Disk expansion creates a larger qcow2, copies and verifies the offline filesystem, then deletes the old disk only after successful expansion and boot. No shrinking. Extra temporary space is required; migration can take several minutes. Memory requires host headroom; CPU count cannot exceed available cores. Background survival depends on Android and root. Microdroid cannot enforce namespace/seccomp service isolation. The experimental kernel still lacks some facilities such as BPF confinement.
Save and recreate only the VM
Closes all Linux sessions. Save your work first. Android is not restarted.

Run plb-install-integration in Linux once. Speaker works in the Bridge fullscreen GUI. Microphone is OFF by default. Choose GUI only or Background; background capture uses an Android microphone service with a Stop action. Android microphone permission is required. Clipboard sharing is text only, up to 64 KiB; start the Linux GUI first.
Could not start background microphone. Open Bridge and check microphone permission.

OFF by default. Background sharing uses root to start a worker under Android shell UID, using its existing clipboard permission. Text only; sensitive Android clips are skipped. No clipboard history is stored. Stops with the runtime. Linux GUI must be running.
Automatic sharing could not start. Check root and runtime.
Automatic sharing worker ready; waiting for clipboard changes and Linux GUI.
Microphone starts only in the Bridge fullscreen GUI.
Microphone is not recording. Open the GUI to connect to Linux.
Microphone is being shared in background.
Microphone sharing needs Android microphone permission.
This runtime requires Android arm64-v8a and Debian arm64.
Match GUI resolution to phone orientation

Select wired, USB or Bluetooth devices already connected to Android. OFF keeps Linux on built-in audio; ON routes Linux streams to the devices below. This forwards audio, not exclusive device ownership. Android apps keep their routing. Reopen the GUI after changes. Classic Bluetooth microphone availability depends on Android exposing an input route.
Use connected devices for Linux audio
The selected audio device is unavailable. Check connected devices.
Multiple audio devices are connected. Select one in Integration.
Android rejected the requested audio route.

The installed crosvm disables direct USB in protected VMs, even with guest USB drivers. USB/Bluetooth audio can instead use Android’s per-stream audio bridge above. No physical peripheral was available for testing.

Choose stock Microdroid or experimental Linux 6.18.57-plb1. Experimental use copies Debian into a separate disk, initially 512 MiB / 1 CPU / CPU graphics. Gunyah memory allocation can terminate the VM under heavier workloads. Android’s kernel and boot partitions stay unchanged; host-failure risk is not zero.

Save Linux work first. Only the current VM will stop. First experimental use copies and verifies the whole disk, requiring time and free device storage. The original disk is retained. Android will not reboot.
Selected: stock Microdroid / original Debian disk
The kernel matches the known SHA-256 and is stored privately. Select and apply its profile.
Import failed. Check the supported 6.18.57-plb1 Image, root access and free space. Other builds or damaged images are rejected.
Stopping VM and preparing profile. The initial copy may take several minutes.
Could not complete the switch. Check kernel installation, storage and root. Select stock Microdroid to reopen the original environment.

Stop this VM and use 512 MiB, 1 CPU, 960 × 540 at 30 fps, Openbox with GPU apps and the GPU viewer. Disk size and other resource settings are retained. This reduces memory pressure; it does not guarantee stability. Reopen the GUI afterwards.

TCP, UDP and DNS without per-app proxy settings, using a TUN interface inside the custom-kernel VM. Android routing and firewall stay unchanged. DNS uses 1.1.1.1 / 8.8.8.8; traffic follows the selected Android app’s network/VPN policy. Background restrictions on that app may block it; choose Bridge for its GUI. No incoming ports, broadcast or arbitrary IP protocols. Ping uses the existing plb-ping relay.
Stop this VM to apply. Open Terminal or GUI again to start it. No Android restart. The guest resolver change lasts only for this boot.
Requires the experimental Linux kernel profile. Stock mode keeps its existing proxy.
Guest TUN is not ready. See /tmp/plb-network.log in Linux.
Guest is running with TUN disabled
VM is stopped. The saved setting applies on its next start.
The network state could not be read. Prepare the runtime and try again.
Android app used for network access
Guest-only TCP, UDP and DNS without per-app proxy configuration. The selected Android app’s network/VPN and background restrictions apply.
